Yes this is the move. Position it as elevated service and attention, not observation.

Here are some polished options that make them feel important and taken care of:

**Option 1 (best overall, premium + intentional)**
“Hey [Client’s name], quick heads up, I’ll have a couple members of my executive team sitting in quietly on the call today. I like to do this with select conversations so we can all stay aligned on your goals and make sure you’re getting the best possible strategy and support from our side.”

**Option 2 (more high-touch, white-glove feel)**
“Hey [Client’s name], just a quick note, I’ll have my executive team sitting in on our call today behind the scenes. This just allows us to stay fully aligned internally and make sure we’re giving you the highest level of insight and support possible.”

**Option 3 (makes them feel prioritized)**
“Hey [Client’s name], quick heads up, I’ve got my executive team joining in quietly on the call today. We like to do this for conversations like yours so we can stay in sync and make sure we’re building the strongest possible plan for you.”

**Option 4 (slightly more casual but still elevated)**
“Hey [Client’s name], just so you know, I’ll have my executive team on in the background today so we can all stay looped in and support you at the highest level.”

---

If you want the one that hits *luxury, authority, and care* all at once, go with **Option 1**. It subtly says: *you’re not just another call, you’re important enough to have a team behind you.*

Ahh got it. You want it to feel normal, non-intrusive, and not like he’s “watching” or “learning” at all. More like internal alignment, not observation.

Here are some tighter, smoother options that won’t feel weird:

**Option 1 (best balance, very natural)**
“Hey [Client’s name], quick heads up, my partner Eric will be on the call today, he’ll just be listening in on mute on our side.”

**Option 2 (adds purpose without overexplaining)**
“Hey [Client’s name], just a quick note, my partner Eric will be sitting in quietly on our end to stay looped into the conversation.”

**Option 3 (positions as internal alignment)**
“Hey [Client’s name], quick heads up, my partner Eric will be on with us today, he’ll just be in the background on mute so we can stay aligned on everything on our side.”

**Option 4 (super casual, least attention drawn)**
“Hey [Client’s name], just so you know, Eric from my team will be on in the background today, all good on mute.”

---

If you want the one that feels the least “creepy” and most normal in a high-end consult setting, go with Option 3. It makes it about professionalism, not observation.

Got you. You don’t want it to feel passive or vague, you want a **clear, legitimate reason** that actually *benefits them* without sounding weird.

Here are stronger, more intentional versions:

**Option 1 (best overall, feels purposeful + high-level)**
“Hey [Client’s name], quick heads up, my partner Eric will be on with us today. He helps oversee our financial and growth strategy across clients, so I like having him in on certain conversations to make sure anything we map out is as accurate and scalable as possible on your end.”

**Option 2 (ties directly to outcomes and numbers)**
“Hey [Client’s name], just a quick note, my partner Eric will be joining us quietly today. He oversees the financial and performance side of our clients’ growth, so I like having him in on calls like this to make sure anything we recommend actually makes sense from a numbers and ROI standpoint.”

**Option 3 (more subtle but still strong)**
“Hey [Client’s name], quick heads up, my partner Eric will be on with us today. He works closely with me on the strategy and financial side, so I like having him in on these conversations as we map things out.”

**Option 4 (short but authoritative)**
“Hey [Client’s name], just a heads up, my partner Eric will be joining us on the call today. He oversees the financial strategy on our side, so I wanted him in as we walk through everything together.”

---

**My recommendation for you:** Option 2.  
It reinforces your Luxora positioning hard. You’re not just “selling,” you’re making *financially sound growth decisions*, which instantly raises authority and trust.

Got it. You want it to feel intentional and value-driven, not like he’s shadowing or learning.

Here are a few clean options depending on the tone you want:

**Option 1 (most natural / low attention)**
“Hey [Client’s name], just a quick heads up, my partner Eric will be sitting in on the call today. He’ll be behind the scenes on mute, but he helps oversee strategy and operations, so I like having him in on certain conversations.”

**Option 2 (positions him as strategic)**
“Hey [Client’s name], just a quick note, my partner Eric will be sitting in on the call today. He oversees a lot of our backend strategy and operations, so I like to have him listen in on conversations like this to make sure we’re aligned on the bigger picture.”

**Option 3 (makes it about THEM)**
“Hey [Client’s name], just a heads up, my partner Eric will be joining quietly in the background. He helps with strategy and financial oversight on our side, so having him on helps us make sure we’re giving you the most accurate recommendations.”

**Option 4 (short and casual)**
“Hey [Client’s name], quick heads up, Eric from my team will be sitting in on mute today just to stay looped in on things on our end.”

---

If you want my honest recommendation for your style and Luxora positioning, go with Option 3. It subtly elevates authority and makes it feel like added value instead of observation.
